# Best portable power station for a CPAP

**My pick: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (about $700).** It has 1,024 Wh of LiFePO4 capacity, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and the lowest noise rating of the group, about 20 dB under 200 W. It recharges from empty in about 49 minutes, and at 24.9 lb it's manageable. Tested Watts estimates about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.7 with it on ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)). Those are research-based estimates, not lab tests. Buy link: [BuyerSheet's CPAP list](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) has "Check on Amazon" and official-store buttons for it. I didn't get a direct product URL.

## Other good options

| Need | Pick | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best value for 2+ nights | **Bluetti AC180** (1,152 Wh) | $449-$499 | Cheapest of the larger units. One source lists $474.05 with code AFF5OFF. Another says the waveform isn't stated in its records, so confirm pure sine with Bluetti. [Buy](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link) |
| CPAP plus whole-home backup | **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** | about $719 | Expandable up to 5 kWh. It's the heaviest at 27.6 lb. See [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/). |
| Small and cheap, no humidifier | **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** (286 Wh) | $279-$299 | 10.4 lb. It covers about one night with the humidifier off. It won't cover a humidified night unless you add the extra battery. See [Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/). |
| Cheapest 1,000 Wh class | **Bluetti Elite 100 V2** | $499 | Rated 4.6 stars across 1,782 ratings. See [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap). |

## Things to know

- **Humidifier:** It roughly doubles your power draw. Runtime estimates vary by source (520 to 720 Wh per humidified night), so check your own machine's wattage label.
- **Pure sine wave:** This is required. Most of these units have it, but check the spec sheet for the one you choose.
- **Jackery caution:** Jackery says its power stations aren't recommended for medical devices, so I'd skip the Explorer line for CPAP unless your CPAP maker approves it.
- **DC cord:** Using your CPAP maker's 12V DC cord can add roughly 10-20% runtime. Don't use a generic car adapter.
- **Outage planning:** Aim for at least two nights of capacity. The formula is nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. For example, 520 Wh × 2 ÷ 0.85 ≈ 1,220 Wh. That's why I lean toward 1,000+ Wh units if you use a humidifier.
- **Prices:** They move often, so confirm at checkout. If you depend on CPAP therapy, check your backup plan with your provider.

If you tell me your CPAP model and whether you use the humidifier, I can narrow this to one pick.
